newsitem.title: USA: Arch Coal sees Q3 charges and mine closing.
newsitem.headline: Arch Coal sees Q3 charges and mine closing.

text.p: Arch Coal Inc said on Friday that it anticipates a one-time charge in the third quarter related to the July 1 merger between Arch Mineral Corp and Ashland Coal Inc to form Arch Coal.
The charge will include severance costs and the writedown of duplicate facilities related to the merger.

In addition, the company said the longwall reserve base at the company's Arch of Kentucky Mine No. 37 in Harlan County, Ky., which will be exhausted near the end of the third quarter, and its substantial contribution to earnings will be lost.

After exhaustion of the longwall reserves, production at Mine No. 37 will be substantially reduced, but the company said the development of a new underground mine in the Darby seam near the No. 37 Mine is being evaluated to partially offset the lost production.

Steven Leer, Arch Coal's president and chief executive officer, said in a statement, "We are excited about the potential synergies and long-term growth opportunities created by the merger, particularly with the combination of two very strong management teams and substantial coal reserves."
The company added that the third quarter is traditionally the weakest for the company due to miners' vacations and higher than normal maintenance costs.
Arch Coal and its independent operating subsidiaries mines, processes and markets coal to electric utilities in the midwestern and eastern United States.
